exposure: No testing or treating for BV (Treat None)
Testing all patients for BV at 36 weeks' gestation and treating if positive (Test Treat)
Empirically treating all patients undergoing cesarean delivery with intravenous metronidazole at time of surgery (Treat All Cesarean)
outcome: Avoidance of postpartum surgical site infection (SSI)
cohort: The study is a model designed to compare strategies for pregnant patients prior to delivery.
finding: Empirically treating all patients for bacterial vaginosis without testing (Treat All Cesarean) was the most effective and least expensive strategy for avoiding postpartum surgical site infections.
mod_finding: Treating all patients undergoing cesarean delivery with intravenous metronidazole at the time of surgery was identified as the most effective and cost-saving strategy to reduce postpartum surgical site infection rates.
